parts.title: My hero
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When people ask me who my hero is, they expect me to name a singer or a footballer. In fact, it is my grandmother. She is not famous, and she has never been on television, but she is the bravest person I know.

My grandmother grew up in a small village with no electricity. When she was fourteen, her father became ill, and she had to leave school to work on the family farm. She got up at four every morning to feed the animals, and she did this for twenty years.

Later, she moved to the city and opened a small shop, where she sold bread and cakes. At first, no one came in, but she kept going. She gave free cake to children after school, and soon their parents began to visit as well. After five years, the shop was the most popular in the street.

She always says, 'You can't change what happens to you, but you can choose what you do about it.' I think about those words whenever something goes wrong. When I am older, I hope that I can be as strong and as kind as she is.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about his hero?
options: She is not famous but very brave
She appeared on television once or twice
She is a well-known singer in town
questions.explanation: She is not famous, but she is the bravest person he knows.

questions.prompt: Why did his grandmother leave school?
options: The school was too far away
She wanted to earn some money
questions.explanation: Her father became ill, so she had to work on the farm.

questions.prompt: How did she attract customers to her shop?
options: She put up bright new posters
She gave free cake to children
She sold cheap bread to everyone
questions.explanation: She gave free cake to children after school.

questions.prompt: What was the shop like after five years?
options: It was still quite empty then
It had to close for a short while
It was the most popular in the street
questions.explanation: After five years, the shop was the most popular in the street.

questions.prompt: What does the writer hope for the future?
options: To become a famous person like others
To open a shop of his own one day
To be strong and kind like her
questions.explanation: He hopes to be as strong and kind as she is.

parts.title: A famous inventor
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Thomas Alva Edison is one of the most famous inventors in history. He was born in 1847 in the United States, and as a child he was always curious about how things worked. [1] His teacher thought he was slow, so his mother took him out of school and taught him at home.

Edison loved to experiment, and at the age of ten, he built a small laboratory in his cellar. [2] Sometimes, his experiments made so much smoke that his family was afraid.

As an adult, he invented many things, including a machine that could record sound. [3] He is probably best known for the electric light bulb, which he improved after trying thousands of materials.

When people asked him about his failures, he answered that he had found a thousand ways that did not work. [4] His strong will is the reason why he became so successful. [5] Today, many of his ideas are still used all over the world.
sentences: He spent all his pocket money on bottles and chemicals.
People could hardly believe that a machine could repeat a voice.
He was also very good at selling his ideas.
In the end, he held more than a thousand patents.
He asked so many questions that the other pupils got tired of him.
Few people have changed the way we live as much as he did.

gaps.explanation: Asking so many questions explains why the teacher thought he was slow.
Spending money on bottles and chemicals goes with the cellar laboratory and smoke.
The machine that could record sound surprised people: they could hardly believe it could repeat a voice.
He held over a thousand patents, which supports his determination.
Few people changed life as much leads to many ideas still being used today.

Tickets [3] sold out in less than an hour, so I was very lucky. I [4] to take my sister, but she is on holiday. Would you [5] to come with me? The show starts at eight, [6] we should leave at six.

parts.title: Heroes of everyday life
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: When we think of heroes, we often imagine soldiers or film stars, but real heroes are all around us. Teachers who stay late to help a child, nurses who work through the night, and neighbours who give food to people in need are all heroes. They do not do these things to become famous, [1] because they care. One woman, who lives in my street, collects clothes [2] families who have lost their homes. She has been doing it for ten years, and she never asks for thanks. Heroes like her teach us that even small acts can make a big difference. [3] you ever feel you are too young or too busy to help, remember that kindness costs nothing. Why not start today? You can help [4] person who needs it, and you will feel proud of [5] you have done. Everybody [6] be a hero in their own way.

gaps.explanation: "Not to become famous, but because they care".

parts.title: A talk about a famous scientist
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Good morning, class. Today, we will learn about Marie Curie, one of the greatest scientists in history. She was born in Poland in eighteen sixty-seven, and her family was very poor. She moved to Paris when she was twenty-four to study at university. There, she met her husband, Pierre, and together they studied a new kind of energy. In nineteen oh three, they won an important prize for physics. Eight years later, she won a second prize, this time for chemistry. She was the first woman to win a prize like this, and she is still the only person to win it in two different sciences. During the war, she helped to build machines that took pictures of bones. She died in nineteen thirty-four, but her work is still helping people today.

gaps.prompt: She moved to Paris at the age of ___
gaps.explanation: She moved to Paris when she was twenty-four.
The second prize was for chemistry.

gaps.prompt: During the war, she built machines for pictures of ___
gaps.explanation: Machines that took pictures of bones.

parts.title: A famous author
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: lucian
turns.text: My guest today is Mirela Cruz, the author of the best-selling Dragon Island books. Mirela, when did you start writing?

turns.speaker: mirela
turns.text: When I was nine. I wrote stories in an old notebook and read them to my little brother. He was my first fan.

turns.speaker: lucian
turns.text: Where do your ideas come from?

turns.speaker: mirela
turns.text: Everywhere. A strange sign, a conversation on a bus, a dream. I always carry a notebook to write them down.

turns.speaker: lucian
turns.text: How do you feel about being famous?

turns.speaker: mirela
turns.text: A bit strange. I'm quite shy, so I don't enjoy being recognised in the street. But I love meeting readers at book signings.

turns.speaker: lucian
turns.text: What is a typical working day?

turns.speaker: mirela
turns.text: I write in the morning for four hours, in a café near my home. In the afternoon, I answer letters or go for a walk.

turns.speaker: lucian
turns.text: What advice would you give to young writers?

turns.speaker: mirela
turns.text: Read as much as you can, and never throw anything away. Even a bad story can have one good sentence.

turns.speaker: lucian
turns.text: Are you planning a new book?

turns.speaker: mirela
turns.text: Yes, a mystery set in a lighthouse. I'm only on chapter two, so it's too soon to say more.
